newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU REPORT CRITICISES WORLD CUP STADIUM CONTRACT - DAILY.
newsitem.headline: EU REPORT CRITICISES WORLD CUP STADIUM CONTRACT - DAILY.

text.p: A report by European Union commissioner Mario Monti has criticised the conditions in which the contract for the biggest stadium for the 1998 soccer World Cup in France was awarded, the daily Le Monde reported on Tuesday.

The report, to be handed to the European Commission on Wednesday, revealed irregularities and especially breaches of article 169 of the Union's treaty and European single market rules, the newspaper said.
Le Monde did not elaborate on Monti's report but said it could force the whole financial set-up of the Paris stadium to be reconsidered and the public cost to be dramatically increased.
"The (French) State...may be summoned to take over a supplementary part of the works and, for a while, the expenses for running the stadium," Le Monde said.
In April 1995, then prime minister Edouard Balladur signed a contract for the building of the stadium with a consortium involving builders Bouygues, Dumez and SGE.
The architect of a rival project, Jean Nouvel, appealed against the decision to the European Commission, leading Brussels to look into the case.

The building of the stadium, which is to host the opening match and the final of the 1998 World Cup, is estimated at more than 2.6 billion francs ($475 million). Public funds account for 1.2 billion francs of this sum and private money will provide the rest.

Le Monde said Sports Minister Guy Drut and the government's official in charge of the stadium, Noel de Saint-Pulgent, went to Brussels on Monday to discuss the matter with the European Commission. ($1=5.473 French Franc)
